mainEntity.name: How much does a Toyota Yaris 1.4 D-4D engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Toyota Yaris 1.4 D-4D engine replacement typically costs between £1,200 and £2,800 for the engine itself, plus labour for supply and fit. Used engines start from around £500, reconditioned units from £1,200, and fully rebuilt engines from £1,500. Used: £500-£1,200. Reconditioned: £1,200-£2,200. Rebuilt: £1,500-£2,800.

mainEntity.name: Why is the Toyota Yaris 1.4 D-4D considered an engine to avoid?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.4 D-4D is widely regarded as the Yaris engine to avoid due to multiple well-documented issues. The water pump is structurally weak and fails without warning, causing rapid overheating and head gasket failure. The engine was also subject to a major recall (2008-2013) for turbo intercooler oil flow issues that could cause serious engine damage. EGR clogging and injector failure are also common.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of water pump failure on a Toyota Yaris 1.4 D-4D?

acceptedAnswer.text: The water pump on the 1ND-TV engine often fails without warning. Look for pink/white crust or a fresh drip at the pump's weep hole or around the pulley, coolant smell, low coolant level, or a small puddle under the front of the engine bay, and overheating gauge climbing rapidly. If you notice any of these, stop driving immediately - continued driving will destroy the head gasket.

mainEntity.name: Was there a recall on the Toyota Yaris 1.4 D-4D?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Toyota recalled approximately 13,000 Yaris 1.4 D-4D models in the UK (2008-2013) as part of a 39,700-vehicle European campaign. The issue was poor airflow from the turbo intercooler, which could allow oil to flow into the combustion chamber and cause serious engine damage. The fix involves repositioning the turbo and updating the ECU. If you own a 2008-2013 Yaris 1.4 D-4D, check whether the recall has been completed - it's free at any Toyota dealer.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Toyota Yaris 1.4 D-4D?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends on your Yaris's condition and value. A typical 2005-2011 Yaris 1.4 D-4D is worth £1,000-£4,000. If the car is in excellent condition with low mileage and the body/interior are good, a replacement engine (£1,200-£2,800) may be justifiable. For cars worth under £2,000, a used engine or repair is often more cost-effective. Always check whether the car has had the recall work completed before committing.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Toyota Yaris 1.4 D-4D engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical Toyota Yaris 1.4 D-4D engine replacement takes 6-9 hours for a specialist workshop, usually completed within 1-2 working days. The 1ND-TV is a relatively compact engine, so access is straightforward compared to larger diesel units. Some specialists offer same-day or next-day fitting.

historyTimeline.h2: Toyota Yaris 1.4 D-4D - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Toyota Yaris 1.4 D-4D joined the Yaris range in 2002 as Toyota's first diesel engine with an aluminium cylinder block. It remained available across three Yaris generations until 2017, making it one of the longest-running diesel options in the supermini class.

milestones.description: Toyota Yaris 1.4 D-4D launched with 1ND-TV engine, 75hp output (XP10 generation)
Yaris Mk2 (XP90) launched; 1ND-TV continues with 90hp output

Yaris Mk3 (XP130) launched; 1ND-TV continues with 90hp, Euro 5 compliant
Facelifted Yaris Mk3 (XP13) retains 1.4 D-4D with 90hp, Euro 6b compliant
Yaris 1.4 D-4D production ends; replaced by hybrid powertrains in Mk4

commonProblems.h2: Toyota Yaris 1.4 D-4D Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Toyota Yaris 1.4 D-4D is widely regarded as the Yaris engine to avoid. While the 1KR-FE and 1NR-FE petrol engines are robust and reliable, the 1ND-TV diesel has multiple well-documented failure points that can make replacement more cost-effective than repair - especially given the low market value of ageing Yaris examples. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Water Pump Failure - Why the Toyota Yaris 1.4 D-4D Overheats Without Warning
problems.rootCause: The 1ND-TV's water pump has a structural weakness - it fails without warning, leading to rapid coolant loss and sudden overheating. The pump failure often damages the head gasket before the driver notices any problem. Toyota has acknowledged this as a design flaw affecting all D-4D engines.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace water pump, flush cooling system, inspect for head gasket damage
Replace head gasket, skim cylinder head if warped, replace water pump
repairOptions.longevity: When overheating has occurred but block is undamaged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded water pump and head gasket components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When overheating has caused bottom-end damage or cylinder head cracking

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Toyota Yaris 1.4 D-4D (2005-2011) is worth £1,000-£4,000, with Mk3 (2011-2017) examples ranging £3,000-£7,000. With water pump replacement costing £250-£700, this is justifiable if caught early. However, head gasket replacement at £800-£2,000 often approaches or exceeds the value of older Yaris examples. For cars worth under £2,000, a used engine or full replacement may be the only sensible option.
problems.recommendation: If you catch the water pump failure before it overheats, replacing the pump is the sensible route. But if the head gasket has already failed - or if the car is worth under £2,000 - a used or reconditioned engine is often the most cost-effective solution. The 1.4 D-4D is simply not worth throwing good money after bad on a high-mileage example.

problems.h4: Turbo Intercooler Recall - Why the Toyota Yaris 1.4 D-4D Was Recalled
problems.rootCause: Poor airflow from the turbo intercooler can allow oil to flow into the combustion chamber, causing serious engine damage. Toyota recalled approximately 13,000 Yaris 1.4 D-4D models in the UK as part of a 39,700-vehicle European campaign.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Inspect intake system, reposition turbo, update ECU if required
repairOptions.longevity: All affected vehicles should have this done

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, with updated intake components
repairOptions.longevity: If recall work was never completed and engine damage has occurred

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a Yaris 1.4 D-4D worth £1,000-£4,000, a full engine replacement is only justifiable if the car is in excellent condition otherwise. Always check whether the recall has been completed on any used Yaris 1.4 D-4D you're considering.
problems.recommendation: If you own a 2008-2013 Yaris 1.4 D-4D and haven't had the recall work done, contact a Toyota dealer immediately - it's free. If the engine has already been damaged by this issue, compare replacement quotes through EnginesMarket rather than paying dealer prices.
problems.cta: -> Check your Yaris 1.4 D-4D recall status and get quotes

problems.h4: EGR & Injector Issues - Why the Toyota Yaris 1.4 D-4D Loses Performance
problems.rootCause: The EGR valve clogs rapidly after 100,000 km (approx 62,000 miles). Injector failure is also common, often caused by running the vehicle on low fuel levels which damages the fuel pressure regulator and injectors.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chemical or manual EGR valve cleaning
Replace EGR valve with new/reconditioned unit
repairOptions.longevity: When cleaning no longer restores performance

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all four injectors with reconditioned units
repairOptions.longevity: When injector failure causes hesitation and poor running

problems.vehicleValueCheck: EGR cleaning at £120-£400 is a sensible maintenance item on any Yaris 1.4 D-4D. Injector replacement at £500-£1,500 is a bigger decision - on a car worth under £2,000, this may be difficult to justify.
problems.recommendation: Regular motorway driving and using premium diesel can help reduce EGR clogging. If you're experiencing hesitation or poor performance, start with an EGR clean before assuming you need a new engine.

finalCta.h4: Don't Let Engine Failure Write Off Your Toyota Yaris 1.4 D-4D
finalCta.paragraph: The Toyota Yaris 1.4 D-4D is one of the most problematic engines Toyota has ever made - and it's a shame, because the Yaris itself is a great little car. Water pump failure, head gasket issues, a major recall, and EGR/injector problems mean this engine can quickly become a money pit.
